narrative.overview:
keek is a workshop with glass walls on the developer's own desktop. The agent works in plain view, in its own room, and the developer can look in at a glance, walk in when called, and walk out again. Every surface keek adds is the frame of that room: it labels who is inside, what they did last, and what came of it. The room itself, the agent's nested Omarchy desktop, is never restyled.

The system borrows everything it can from the host. Omarchy's bar, Hyprland's borders and 8px rounding, JetBrains Mono and the theme palette carry over unchanged, so a Session Card reads as one more Omarchy window with a footer, not as an app. keek's own vocabulary is small and strict: one footer, one Verdict panel, one toast, one cursor. Density is that of a status bar, not a dashboard; a glance answers "is it progressing, is it stuck, does it need me".

Colour is reserved for meaning. Navy and parchment carry everything at rest. Orange appears only when the developer is needed, green, coral and yellow only for Check outcomes, and each session's cursor colour only where it ties the card to its cursor.

The approved comps live in `design/comps/` and in the design canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/LxCSK6QwgvUrNBKL8ftXzq). Values below are measured from those comps on the Cumulus theme; on any other theme the colours follow that theme (see Colors).
keyCharacteristics: Native to Omarchy: host bar, borders, rounding and type, no keek chrome on the agent's desktop.
Window and footer join into one Session Card.
Status-bar density: label over value, one line each.
Colour by meaning only; state also readable by shape and word.
Flat: borders and a dim scrim make depth, never shadows.

rules.name: The Orange Means You Rule
rules.body: Needs-you Orange marks a Help Request only. Never use it for warnings, skipped Checks or Partly verified.

rules.name: The Session Colour Rule
rules.body: A session's colour appears on its cursor, its footer's top edge and its arrow glyph, and nowhere else. It never colours state, text or buttons.

rules.name: The Outcome Palette Rule
rules.body: Green, coral and yellow belong to Check outcomes. A Verdict's colour is the colour of the outcome that decided it.

rules.name: The Tabular Clock Rule
rules.body: Elapsed, Ran and percentages use tabular numerals so a running clock never shifts its column.

rules.name: The Label Over Value Rule
rules.body: Footer columns are a dim label line over a bold value line. Never put a label and value on one line.

rules.name: The Flat Host Rule
rules.body: If Omarchy's own surfaces don't cast a shadow, keek's don't either.

rules.name: The One Card Rule
rules.body: The footer overlaps the window's bottom 8px, draws its side and bottom border in the window's current border colour, and changes with it: inactive at rest, active during a Takeover, orange for a Help Request.

dos: Do take the bar, borders, rounding (8px), gaps (24px) and font from the host so the Session Card reads as an Omarchy window.
Do pair every outcome colour with an icon shape and a word.
Do keep the footer to label-over-value columns at 12px, with values in bold.
Do show "Needs fixes" with the attempt count ("attempt 1 of 3") so a retry reads as progress.
Do check new work against the comps in `design/comps/` before calling it done.
donts: Don't restyle or overlay the agent's nested desktop while it runs; keek draws only around it.
Don't call a Verdict "Fail" or show a bare red failure state.
Don't use Needs-you Orange for anything but a Help Request.
Don't add shadows, gradients or a second font family.
Don't put the session start time on screen; it lives in the Evidence file names.
Don't steal focus, pop over the developer's editor or animate while nothing needs them.
